The binomial theorem

Expanding (a+b)n by repeated multiplication quickly becomes tedious. The binomial theorem gives every term directly: the coefficients are the binomial coefficients (nk) — the numbers in row n of Pascal's triangle — while the power of a falls from n to 0 as the power of b rises from 0 to n. Enter two terms such as 2x and −3 to get the full expansion, or ask for a single term of a large power.

Try changing the input

Change the second term from 3 to −3: the coefficients keep their sizes but alternate in sign, because odd powers of a negative number are negative.

Formula and variables

(a+b)n=∑k=0n(nk)a n−kb k,Tk+1=(nk)a n−kb k
SymbolMeaning
a,bThe two terms, each a single monomial (numbers and variables with whole-number powers).
nWhole-number power.
(nk)=n!k!(n−k)!Binomial coefficient; the expansion has n+1 terms.
Tk+1The general term: term number k+1 uses bk.

Worked example

Expand (2x−3)3

Step 1 — Coefficients (row 3 of Pascal's triangle)

1, 3, 3, 1.

Step 2 — Terms

1(2x)3+3(2x)2(−3)+3(2x)(−3)2+1(−3)3

Step 3 — Simplify

8x3−36x2+54x−27

Assumptions, domain and rounding

  • Each of a and b must be a single term (no + or − inside); variables allowed are x, y, z, a, b and t.
  • The full expansion is available for n≤30; a single term can be found for n≤1000.
  • All coefficients are exact (BigInt integers or fractions).
